title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and spent about six months in jail after Fargo, North Dakota police wrongly charged her with bank theft. She was held for nearly four months in Tennessee awaiting extradition and about two more months in North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records showing she was in Tennessee at the time of the fraud, and she was released on Christmas Eve. Lipps says she lost her home, car, and personal property while in custody.

Lipps has filed a federal lawsuit seeking $10 million in damages from the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck. The suit claims police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and surveillance video without enough investigation or probable cause. It also says Fargo lacked proper policies, training, and supervision for facial recognition use. The city declined to comment on pending litigation. The lawsuit seeks accountability and damages, but no further court dates are mentioned.
